findings.text: follow-on: option_key returns '<family>:<model>', which is not guaranteed unique across offered candidates - two configured backends sharing the same harness command (hence the same family) and the same model value collapse to one key. Because build_questions stores criteria_entries in a dict keyed by option_key and pick() resolves with next(c for c in offered if option_key(c) == choice), the second such backend is silently dropped from the offered options and can never be selected. The docstring's claim that the fallback 'keeps every offered key distinct' holds only when the models differ, and the new test cannot detect the collision because it builds `{option_key(c): c.backend for c in offered}`, which collapses duplicate keys before comparing. Non-blocking provided no live flight config declares two backends with the same command and model; if such a config exists the pair-key contract loses a backend. If it ever becomes one, keying by backend (which is what dispatch launches) would keep both.

follow-on: the questions instructions now tell Jev that 'each option's key names its lane and its model joined with a colon', but option_key substitutes the backend name for the second part when a candidate names no model, so a modelless candidate's offered key names its backend rather than a model. The wording is a closer match to the delivered contract than before, but it overstates it for the fallback case. Non-blocking; the key still parses as '<lane>:<something>'.
